_read_me: Everything in the cost report that is a judgement rather than a price or a constant read from code. Each number says what it is. The page lets you change any of them live; change them here to change the default.

light.label: Light
light.note: a few times a month, under ten

normal.label: Normal
normal.note: files a bunch, reads a bunch, forwards an email now and then, WhatsApp sometimes

llmHeavy.label: LLM heavy
llmHeavy.note: lives in WhatsApp and the composer, asks a lot, looks things up

badActor.label: Bad actor
badActor.note: scripted, sits on every cap the code has, and sends dumps where the code has none
badActor._why: Caps from code: 200 photos a day, 100 voice notes and 3,600 seconds a day, 100 emails a day, 3 searches and 3 reads a turn. WhatsApp's 200 a day is 029's planned cap. Dumps and questions have no cap of their own, so 500 and 200 a day stand in for a script running slowly; the daily turn count and budget hold it back where the code has them. A row typed into a section costs nothing.

turn._read_me: What one model turn looks like. Calibrated against the principle evals (small contexts) and the 2026-09-17 decision's per-dump range (production contexts).

nightly._read_me: One pass per thread and member a night. Up to 100 notes, and the member's dumps since their last pass there, at most 40 of 500 characters; a few on a usual day. The system prompt has three variants, each cached.

eval._read_me: The principle evals run on fresh accounts with almost no context; this is the turn shape that reproduces them, for the calibration check.

storage._read_me: Bytes per kept thing, in MB. A photo is three R2 objects: the original, a 2048px rendition and a 400px thumb.

infra._read_me: Railway is billed on measured CPU, memory, egress and volume. These are estimates of the provisioned shape at each scale, not a bill; replace railwayActual with the figure from Railway's usage page and the report uses it at the smallest scale.
